claim: OpenCV is hard-wired: CameraWorker.create always spawns opencv_camera_worker_method; there is no backend abstraction, and determine_backend.py only selects an OpenCV videoio API (DSHOW/V4L2/AVFoundation).
how_verified: read-code; grep for gige|aravis|harvester|genicam|ptp|1588|spinnaker|pypylon|vimba over skellycam/, skellycam-ui/src, pyproject.toml returned no hits

claim: Cross-camera sync is a frame-count lock-step gate: a camera may grab only when all_ready and its frame_count <= all others; grab() and retrieve() then run back-to-back in the same process with no inter-camera barrier between them (contrary to the opencv_get_frame docstring).
how_verified: read-code; ran-test (test_camera_orchestrator.py passed in pytest run, log research/skellycam-arch-pytest.log)

claim: Additional barriers: startup waits (draining frames via read()) until orchestrator.all_ready; recording start waits until all cameras are recording.

The frame-number is a host-side counter incremented per successful retrieve, not a device frame ID; a text overlay is drawn into the image before SHM write and recording, so it appears in recorded video.
check_framerate_reset hard-codes a 30 fps target and recreates the cv2.VideoCapture after 30 consecutive slow frames.

CameraConfig fields: camera_id, camera_index (cv2 index, must be unique), camera_name, use_this_camera, resolution, color_channels=3, pixel_format='RGB' (TODO/unused), exposure_mode, exposure (OpenCV log2), framerate, rotation, capture_fourcc='MJPG', writer_fourcc='X264'; no backend or device-address field.

Frame dtype is {frame_metadata, image uint8[H,W,color_channels]}; metadata has camera_info, frame_number, timebase_mapping and 9 lifecycle int64 timestamps all written from time.perf_counter_ns(); there is no device/PTP timestamp or device frame-id field.
how_verified: read-code; ran-test (research/scripts/skellycam_arch_verify.py printed dtype field names; backend_protocol_prototype.py confirmed 'device_timestamp_ns' absent)

claim: Host timestamps map to UTC via one TimebaseMapping sample created with CameraGroupIPC (camera-group creation), not at recording start as the docs state.

Downstream consumers assume 3-channel BGR uint8 (JPEG encode, cv2.VideoWriter default isColor, PyAV bgr24); mono (color_channels=1) is inconsistent: frame dtype holds (H,W,1) but CameraConfig.image_shape is (H,W), which recording validation compares against decoded video frames.
how_verified: read-code; ran-test (skellycam_arch_verify.py [1]: color_channels=1 -> dtype image shape (48,64,1) vs image_shape (48,64))

claim: Each camera's SHM ring defaults to 1 GiB / frame itemsize slots: 388 frames at 1280x720 BGR, 155 at 1920x1200, 71 at 2448x2048, 29 at 4096x3000.

Device detection uses cv2_enumerate_cameras via detect_available_cameras, returning CameraDeviceInfo(index,name,vid,pid,path,backend_id,backend_name) with camera_id hashed from path/vid-pid; exposed at POST /skellycam/camera/detect; the UI builds CameraConfig from (camera_id, index, name) only.

Per-camera timestamp CSVs auto-map every FRAME_LIFECYCLE_TIMESTAMPS_DTYPE field to a column minus the host recording_start_time_ns, so device-clock timestamps must be stored in a separate sub-record with explicit columns; the multiframe CSV's inter_camera.frame_grab_range.ms uses host grab midpoints.
Frame metadata reaches the finalizer via VideoRecorder.video_frame_metadata -> RecordingFinishedMessage -> RecordingFinalizer, so new metadata fields (e.g. device_timing) need no new IPC.

beartype_this_package() enforces all annotations at runtime; a typing.Protocol used as a hint must be @runtime_checkable (else BeartypeDecorHintPep3119Exception at decoration); a conforming fake backend passes and a non-conforming object raises BeartypeCallHintParamViolation.

Existing test suite: 171 passed, 15 failed, 4 errors; most failures are beartype rejecting MagicMock or int/float mismatches; process hangs after the summary. MockVideoCapture lacks grab()/retrieve().
how_verified: ran-test: timeout 90 <scratch venv>/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q -rfE --tb=line skellycam/tests (log research/skellycam-arch-pytest.log)

claim: cv2.cvtColor(bayer, code, dst=frame_rec_array.image[0]) debayers directly into the recarray image view (shares memory, no extra copy); measured ~40 us at 640x480 and ~0.18 ms at 2448x2048 on this machine (OpenCV 4.12.0).
For an RGGB mosaic (red at pixel (0,0)), OpenCV COLOR_BayerBG2BGR yields red while COLOR_BayerRG2BGR yields blue, so the PFNC-name-to-OpenCV-code table must map by layout rather than by name.
SHM frame dtype is fixed at camera-group start from extracted configs; check_for_new_config applies settings but does not resize frame_rec_array or SHM.

Docs/code discrepancies: architecture.mdx claims a second multiframe SHM buffer and JPEG quality 80; code reads per-camera rings directly and uses quality 60; precise-timestamps.mdx links a non-existent timebase_mapping path.
create_camera_frame_csv_row_recarray is unused dead code with a pre+pre midpoint bug and non-existent column names.
